contexts.text: Hence came their statues in the open air.
The externals of their worship were statues, etc.
The statue seen by Nebuchadnezzar () = that from true worship comes at last such worship as is called Babel... As also the statue of gold which Nebuchadnezzar set up ().
A pillar (). ( = truth which is the ultimate of order in the Natural. AC 3727:3.)
The statue () = the successive times of the Church (that is, the golden, silver, copper, and iron ages). AC 3021:8.
The head of the statue () = celestial things; the breast, spiritual or rational things; and so on.
That the affection of truth perishes, is signified by Lot's wife made a statue of salt. AC 2455.
The statues of the house of the sun () = the worship of self.

A statue () is here expressed in the Hebrew by a word which means a standing still; and not by one which means a statue erected for worship, or for a sign, or for a witness; so that by the statue of salt is here signified that the truth signified by Lot's wife stood vastated.
He set it for a pillar () = a holy boundary; thus the ultimate of order.

For in the most ancient times, stones were placed at their boundaries, which marked the sion... and were for a sign and witness that the boundaries were there... The Ancients began to account these stones holy... and called them pillars; and in this way pillars were introduced into worship, and they erected them in the places where they had their groves, and afterwards where they had their temples, and also anointed them with oil... The Most Ancients were instructed that stones = truth... This is why pillars = a holy boundary, thus truth, which is the ultimate of order in man...
That the pillars were erected for a sign, and for a witness, and also for worship; and that they = a holy boundary, or truth in man's Natural. Illustrated.
The twelve pillars () = the truth which is from good in worship.
A representative of truth was established by the stones of the altar; and they were forbidden to represent it by pillars, lest thereby truth should be separated from good... (). AC 10643:4.
Nevertheless they did erect pillars, and thereby represented things contrary to order. Illustrated.
The pillars among the gentiles = falsities, and therefore it was commanded that they should be destroyed. Illustrated.
Where thou anointedst a pillar () = where the good of truth is and its boundary. A pillar = a holy boundary; thus the ultimate of order; and consequently truth.
Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar () = such truth and the derivative worship... A pillar = worship from truth.
A pillar () = truth... Both the heap and the pillar were for a sign or for a witness; here, for a sign of the limit. Explained.
To set with thee () = to conjoin.
Jacob set up a pillar in the place where He spake with him, a pillar of stone () = what is holy of truth in that Divine state.

The pillars erected in ancient times were either for a sign, for a witness, or for worship. Those for worship were anointed, and were then holy, and worship was held there... This ritual derived its representation from the fact that in the most ancient times stones were set up on the boundaries between families of nations, lest they should pass over them to do one another evil... That they should not pass beyond them to do evil was to them a law of nations. And, as the stones were on the boundaries, the Most Ancients... when they saw them, thought about truths which are the ultimates of order... At last, their descendants... began to regard these stones as holy, pouring libations upon them, and anointing them with oil; and they were then called pillars, and were used for worship.

In the Ancient Church, the pillars served them as means of attaining to internal worship. Explained... Hence it was that the Ancients had pillars for worship in their temples, groves, and forests, and upon the hills and mountains. AC 10643.
Jacob set up a pillar upon her grave () = what is holy of spiritual truth that would be raised up there. A pillar = what is holy of truth.
To set before () = insinuation.

Two statues, partly of flesh, and partly of stone, appear in the boundary of the created universe, in front towards the left, which are said to swallow those who think of what the Divine was doing from eternity. Explained. TCR 31:end. SE 3481:end, Explained.
They who hold to what is internal...
A pillar of salt = disjunction from truth.
Thou shalt break in pieces their statues () = that the falsities of worship are to be put aside.

Twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel () = a representative of the Lord's Divine Human as to the Divine truth which is from Him in its whole complex. A pillar = a representative of the Lord's Divine Human as to truth; because by an altar is signified a representative of it as to good; and a pillar, in the representative sense, = the Holy of truth which is from the Lord. References.
Under State, see this reference.
The head of the statue () = the first state of the Church; the breast and arms, the second; and so on.

Ye shall break their statues () = that the falsities of evil are to be dissipated. Statues = representatives of the worship of the Lord from truths; and, in the opposite sense, of idolatrous worship from falsities.
The statues (or pillars) which the ancients placed upon mountains and in groves = Divine truth; for the pillars were stones... AC 10643:3, Illustrated.
In these passages, pillars = worship from truths, because a stone = Divine truth; and a pillar anointed with oil, Divine truth from Divine good.
They establish (the inference) that...
They who hold to (this idea).
These four Churches are meant by the statue (). AR 913:3. CL 78. TCR 760.
You were not created statues, but men.
Its appointed state. AR 562.
They saw them... as statues and carved idols, with an assembly kneeling round them.
Take heed lest your minds... should become statues of salt.
He who confirms himself in a plurality of gods... becomes like a statue made with movable joints...

I saw instead of the tents two statues in the likeness of men, made of the dust of the earth (which represented their faith as queen and charity as her servant). Described. A shower from Heaven soaked both the statues (causing them) to boil up... and become heaps... like sepulchral mounds.
If man were to stand... like a sculptured statue with movable joints, and wait for influx...
I say. No more than a statue, and not no more than a beast. Explained.
If man were deprived of free will in spiritual things, he would be no longer a man, but only a statue.

(A dream of a theatre consisting of statues of a brown colour, one or two of which moved themselves, as if to commence a theatrical play.) SE 1881. (The statues represented those who live in externals only. SE 1882.)
Men who aspire to an immortality of fame... by means of sepulchral statues, etc.
Hence (the Dutch) do not tolerate in their places of worship either statues, images, or pictures.
(These common people) spoke almost (like) lifeless statues.
(Polhem) made statues (there, for magical purposes).
The statue () = the state of the Church as to good and truth, from its first time to its last, (which was) when the Lord came into the world. AE 176:2. AE 237:11.
That they anointed stones set up for pillars. Illustrated.
A pillar to Jehovah in the border thereof () = the worship of the Lord from the truths of faith; a pillar = worship from the truths of faith. AE 654:8.
Sun-statues () = worship from natural truths.
Their altar = worship from evil; their statues, worship from falsity, and therefore Hell. AE 391:25.
Sun-statues () = idolatrous worship from falsities of doctrine.

The head of the statue () = the Most Ancient Church. Explained... Its breast and arms = the Ancient Church. Explained... Its belly and thighs = the Church which succeeded the Ancient spiritual Church, which may be called spiritual natural. Explained... Its legs and feet, which were part iron and part clay = he Israelitish and Jewish Church. Explained. AE 577:5.
The altar and twelve pillars () = all truths from good by which the Church exists.

He shall bring down the pillars of strength to the earth ()... = that all worship from truths will be destroyed. For pillars = holy worship from truths; and as all power is of truth from good, they are called pillars of strength.
Under Statute, see this reference.

The statue () describes the state of the Church which becomes Babylon, from its beginning to its end. Explained... Its head = wisdom; and gold, the good of love to the Lord. That the toes of its feet were part of iron and part of clay = that the last state of that Church would be destitute of all good of love and of all wisdom. Explained... The new Church which will then be established... is described in (). Here... kingdom = the Church, in like manner as a man, in the form of which the statue was.

The consummation of the Church from its first foundation to its last is described by the statue ()... the first Church, which was before the Flood, by the gold; the second, after the Flood, by the silver; the third, which was Israelitish... by the brass; and the fourth which was Christian, by the iron mixed with clay. CanonsNC 43. Trinity. 7. 6.
